as_told.title: Dobrynin raises UFOs with US presidential adviser

plain: In the 1960s, the Soviet ambassador to Washington, Anatoly Dobrynin, privately asked an American official why everyone was so worked up about UFOs. The official was Harald Malmgren, an adviser to presidents Kennedy, Johnson, Nixon and Ford, and he tells Michels about it himself as something he was part of. "I have never talked about this," he says. Dobrynin "did ask at one time, why is everyone so excited about these unidentified flying objects?" Michels later retells it in another episode in his own words, calling the two men friends and saying that Dobrynin brought up UFOs and "said he was very interested." So the source is Malmgren's own memory, with the host repeating it. If it happened, it would show the Soviets paying attention to American interest in UFOs at the height of the Cold War.
